rationale: Mozilla's standalone Readability.js library (v0.6.0, Apache-2.0, 2,812 lines in Readability.js) extracts structured article content from arbitrary HTML documents. It powers Firefox Reader View. The library implements two primary concerns relevant to the Veridian pipeline: (1) JSON-LD / Schema.org extraction via its _getJSONLD method (Readability.js lines 1658-1773) which parses application/ld+json scripts, validates @context against schema.org, filters by jsonLdArticleTypes regex, and extracts title/byline/excerpt/siteName/datePublished; and (2) fuzzy string matching via _textSimilarity (used at lines 1726-1728 to disambiguate JSON-LD name vs. headline fields against the document title, threshold >0.75 similarity). The library is classified tier B rather than S or A because: it is a general-purpose article extractor, not a scraping pipeline component; its JSON-LD extraction is limited to Schema.org Article subtypes (not general JSON-LD); its fuzzy matching is a single utility function, not a full dedupe/matching engine; it has zero overlap with browser-automation, script-generation, self-healing, stealth, queue, or fulltext-search pipeline concerns. The 130 test-pages directory provides strong coverage across diverse real-world sites (cnn, nytimes, bbc, guardian, etc.), and the test suite runs each page through both jsdom and JSDOMParser backends. No architecture or design documents beyond the README API reference exist. The library is not a declared core candidate (heritage=false) and sits comfortably as a B-tier reference: high-quality implementation of a narrow concern useful as a subordinate component.
limitations: JSON-LD extraction is limited to Schema.org Article subtypes only, not general JSON-LD extraction
Fuzzy matching is limited to a single _textSimilarity method for disambiguating name vs. headline, not a general dedupe engine
No overlap with browser-automation, script-generation, self-healing, stealth, queue, or fulltext-search concerns
Library performs DOM manipulation (mutates input) unless caller manually clones the document
No bundled dependency injection for network requests (expects a pre-parsed DOM document)
The isProbablyReaderable helper is explicitly noted as producing both false positives and false negatives
No architecture or design documentation beyond API reference in README
